_note: Bolt tightening torques transcribed from the two reference charts the company works from: the grade table "Torque chart in Nm with bolt grade" (grades 3.6–12.9) and the SPX Bolting Systems stud chart (grade "B7"). Each row names its basis — the three sets assume different friction and stress ratios and are NOT interchangeable. Rows that disagree with their own neighbours are carried as printed but flagged unverified so they take the engineer-confirmation path. wrench_status is below_range when the torque falls under our smallest wrench and above_range when it exceeds our largest (39000 Nm).

_bases.oiled-62: Untreated, oil-smeared threads · friction coefficient μ = 0.125 · torque corresponds to approx. 62% of tensile bolt stress. Recommended maximum tightening torque, company torque chart.
_bases.oiled-90: Untreated, oil-smeared threads · friction coefficient μ = 0.14 · torque corresponds to approx. 90% of tensile bolt stress. Starred large sizes on the company torque chart.
_bases.b7-65-moly: ASTM A193 B7 stud at 65% of yield with molybdenum-disulphide / graphite lubricant — SPX Bolting Systems chart. Friction varies; in extreme cases check with the bolt manufacturer.

rows.note: Printed as 7 Nm on the company chart, which is below the same row’s grade 6.8 figure (7.7 Nm) — the sequence says it should be nearer 10 Nm. Transcribed as printed; the engineer must confirm against the hard copy.
